claims.text: Nitrogen doping of a platinum-group-metal-based high-entropy-alloy catalyst enhances ethanol-oxidation performance.
The appropriate baseline is the same platinum-group-metal-based HEA nanoscale catalyst without nitrogen doping.
Nitrogen dopants occupy sites within the HEA structure.
Nitrogen dopants modify the local electronic properties of the HEA.
The nitrogen-induced electronic modification changes the adsorption energies of ethanol and ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Nitrogen doping produces moderate adsorption energies for ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Moderate intermediate adsorption facilitates complete 12-electron oxidation of ethanol.
The nitrogen-induced adsorption profile reduces catalyst degradation and leaching.
The nitrogen-induced adsorption profile increases selectivity toward complete ethanol oxidation.
The nitrogen-doped catalyst will exhibit higher ethanol-oxidation current density than the undoped catalyst under identical conditions.
The nitrogen-doped catalyst will exhibit greater selectivity toward full oxidation products, including CO2, than the undoped catalyst.
The nitrogen-doped catalyst will have better long-term operational stability than the undoped catalyst.
The proposed enhancement applies primarily at moderate ethanol concentrations and under standard electrolyte conditions.
At extremely high ethanol concentrations or in substantially altered solvent systems, nitrogen doping may not provide the predicted benefits.
